FINA 101.description: Course will provide a basic framework for student personal financial management while in college. Topics include money management skills, banking, credit cards, creditworthiness, credit reports, students loans, identity theft, and basic taxes.
FINA 101.subject: FINA
FINA 101.title: Introduction to Personal Finance

FINA 301.description: The role of money in the market economy. Commercial banks, the Federal Reserve System, and monetary policy.
FINA 301.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 221 and ECON 222, or ECON 224.
FINA 301.subject: FINA
FINA 301.title: Money and Banking

FINA 333.description: In-depth introduction to the world of finance. Interaction of individuals and companies with financial markets.
FINA 333.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ECON 224 or ECON 221 and ECON 222, ACCT 222.
FINA 333.subject: FINA
FINA 333.title: Finance and Markets

FINA 341.description: Introduction to decision making under uncertainty and overview of how carious markets allow individuals and organizations to diversify risk. Includes measurement of risk, behavioral bias in decision making under uncertainty, diversification of risk, the role of capital in ensuring performance, moral hazard, adverse selection, insurance pricing, and applications to public policy issues such as health care, catastrophe risk, and safety regulation.
FINA 341.subject: FINA
FINA 341.title: Management of Risk and Insurance

FINA 363.description: Basic concepts of finance related to decision making.
FINA 363.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ECON 221 or ECON 224; C or better in ACCT 225 or RETL 261; C or better in STAT 201, STAT 205, STAT 206, STAT 509, STAT 511, STAT 515, or MATH 511.
FINA 363.subject: FINA
FINA 363.title: Introduction to Finance

FINA 364.description: A study of the functions and operations of financial institutions and their relationships to the commercial banking system and the general economy. Attention is devoted to savings institutions, insurance companies, rural and urban real estate credit, consumer credit, and associated topics.
FINA 364.subject: FINA
FINA 364.title: Financial Institutions

FINA 365.description: Analysis of business investment and financing decisions.
FINA 365.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 363.
FINA 365.subject: FINA
FINA 365.title: Corporate Financial Analysis

FINA 366.description: Real estate analysis and administration; basic principles, concepts, terminology, and institutional factors related to real estate decisions in the urban environment. This course fulfills a pre-examination requirement of the South Carolina Real Estate licensing law (30-hour approved course).
FINA 366.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 363, FINA 333, RETL 421, or HTMT 421.
FINA 366.subject: FINA
FINA 366.title: Introduction to Real Estate and Urban Development

FINA 367.description: Concepts, methodologies, and analytical tools used in urban real estate analysis.
FINA 367.subject: FINA
FINA 367.title: Real Estate Market Analysis

FINA 369.description: Life insurance, health insurance, wills, trusts, Social Security, stocks, bonds, real estate, mutual funds, and other uses of funds.
FINA 369.subject: FINA
FINA 369.title: Personal Finance

FINA 401.description: Critical personal finance skills for the graduating senior, including budgeting, banking, personal taxes, insurance, saving for retirement, and more.
FINA 401.subject: FINA
FINA 401.title: Personal Finance for the Graduating Senior

FINA 442.description: Individual financial management of economic losses caused by premature death, disability, and old age; functional aspects of life-health insurer management.
FINA 442.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 341 and FINA 363.
FINA 442.subject: FINA
FINA 442.title: Life and Health Insurance

FINA 443.description: Functional aspects of property-liability insurer management and operations including detailed treatment of pricing, risk assessment, marketing, investment, contract design, financial statement analysis, and regulation.
FINA 443.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 341 and FINA 363.
FINA 443.subject: FINA
FINA 443.title: Property and Liability Insurance

FINA 444.description: Tools and concepts used by corporations in managing all types of risk with a focus on the use of derivatives and insurance. Analysis of when risk reduction is beneficial.
FINA 444.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 341, FINA 363, and MGSC 291.
FINA 444.subject: FINA
FINA 444.title: Corporate Risk Management

FINA 445.description: Management of employer-sponsored benefits, especially group life, health, and retirement plans; emphasis on plan design and administration, cost, funding, regulation, and tax considerations.
FINA 445.subject: FINA
FINA 445.title: Employee Benefits

FINA 446.description: Innovative insurance operations to compete in the modern world.
FINA 446.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 341 and FINA 363.
FINA 446.subject: FINA
FINA 446.title: Insurance Operations

FINA 462.description: Examines the important role that risk management, insurance, and finance have in dealing with climate change risk and how climate change risk affects financial markets and financial institutions.
FINA 462.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in either FINA 341, FINA 365, or FINA 469.
FINA 462.subject: FINA
FINA 462.title: Climate Change Risk Management, Insurance, and Finance

FINA 463.description: Application of financial concepts and tools to corporate decisions.
FINA 463.subject: FINA
FINA 463.title: Case Studies in Corporate Finance

FINA 464.description: Explores the history, current environment, and near term outlook of financial innovation (FinTech), focusing on applications of Blockchain technology and Machine Learning tools. The course is designed to provide hands on experience in writing a “smart contract” using a blockchain and in applying machine learning tools.
FINA 464.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 365 or FINA 465 or FINA 469.
FINA 464.subject: FINA
FINA 464.title: Financial Innovation

FINA 465.description: Fundamental principles underlying the employment of bank funds. Allocation of funds among the various classes of loans and investments to bank operating costs and to changing bank practices.
FINA 465.subject: FINA
FINA 465.title: Commercial Bank Practice and Policy

FINA 466.description: Analysis and decision-making; return and risk; financing; tax implications; pricing and investment strategies.
FINA 466.subject: FINA
FINA 466.title: Real Estate Investment Fundamentals

FINA 467.description: The nature and importance of credit in real estate development and operations; legal framework, sources of mortgage funds, role of public and private financial institutions.
FINA 467.subject: FINA
FINA 467.title: Real Estate Finance

FINA 468.description: Traditional appraisal concepts and methodologies; appraisal process, real property analysis.
FINA 468.subject: FINA
FINA 468.title: Real Estate Appraisal

FINA 469.description: Conceptual and analytical framework for formulating investment policies, analyzing securities, and constructing portfolios.
FINA 469.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 363 and MGSC 291.
FINA 469.subject: FINA
FINA 469.title: Investment Analysis and Portfolio Management

FINA 470.description: This course focuses on the analysis of financial statements for profitability and risk assessment and for firm and segment valuation.
FINA 470.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ACCT 225 and ACCT 226 and FINA 363.
FINA 470.subject: FINA
FINA 470.title: Financial Statement Analysis

FINA 471.description: Options, forward and futures contracts, and swap contracts are analyzed, along with their uses in risk management, portfolio management, and corporate financing. Markets where these contracts trade will be examined.
FINA 471.subject: FINA
FINA 471.title: Derivative Securities

FINA 472.description: Hands-on experience in investment analysis; managing a real portfolio, decision-making in the design of a portfolio management process, asset allocation, security selection, and risk management. Enrollment in this course requires a special permission from the instructor.
FINA 472.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MGSC 291.
FINA 472.subject: FINA
FINA 472.title: Student-Managed Investments

FINA 473.description: Exploring conflicts of interest between corporate managers and the providers of capital, and studying various mechanisms to address the misalignment of incentives and therefore restore firm value.
FINA 473.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 363.
FINA 473.subject: FINA
FINA 473.title: Corporate Governance and Agency Conflicts

FINA 474.description: Examination of key legal areas of real estate practice including the legal principles applied to real estate investment, brokerage, operations and development.
FINA 474.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 366.
FINA 474.subject: FINA
FINA 474.title: Real Estate Law

FINA 475.description: Examine fundamental principles of fixed-income securities and fixed-income valuation models.
FINA 475.subject: FINA
FINA 475.title: Fixed Income Securities

FINA 476.description: Examines the foundations of capitalism and why it has prevailed over alternative systems. Topics include the justification of private property, distribution of wealth, profit motive, source of wealth creation, and others.
FINA 476.subject: FINA
FINA 476.title: Foundations of Capitalism

FINA 477.description: Introduction to the real estate development process with emphasis on analyzing the feasibility of design, location, and construction. Students will learn to identify and evaluate critical issues related to market and site feasibility, financial feasibility, planning, acquisition, and operation of viable real estate projects.
FINA 477.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 366.
FINA 477.subject: FINA
FINA 477.title: Real Estate Development

FINA 478.description: Survey of how financial institutions with billions of dollars under management design and implement their investment programs.
FINA 478.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 469.
FINA 478.subject: FINA
FINA 478.title: Foundations of Institutional Investing

FINA 479.description: Survey of private capital markets and basic principles associated with deal origination, transaction modeling, execution, monitoring, and exit/sales process
FINA 479.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 469.
FINA 479.subject: FINA
FINA 479.title: Private Capital Markets

FINA 480.description: Global institutional investment in real estate; international capital markets viewed from the perspective of real estate investment and finance professionals.
FINA 480.subject: FINA
FINA 480.title: Global Real Estate Capital Markets

FINA 490.description: 1-3 credit hours for up to 9 credit hours total.
FINA 490.subject: FINA
FINA 490.title: Special Topics in Finance

FINA 499.description: Supervised work experience as approved by department. Generally three hours of academic credit, but upon special request of supervising professor and approval of appropriate area director, an internship may carry a maximum of six credit hours. Pass-Fail only. Internship contract required.
FINA 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 363, cumulative GPA of 2.8.
FINA 499.subject: FINA
FINA 499.title: Business Internship in Finance, Real Estate and Insurance

FINA 589.description: Application of machine learning and AI techniques to financial problems in investment, corporate finance, and banking.
FINA 589.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Undergraduates: C or better in FINA 469.
FINA 589.subject: FINA
FINA 589.title: Machine Learning and AI: Applications to Finance

FINA 666.description: An overview of real estate in both the public and private sectors that serves as the basis for advanced study in the various disciplines of real estate and urban development. No prior knowledge of the field is assumed.
FINA 666.subject: FINA
FINA 666.title: Real Estate and Urban Development

FINA 737.description: Derivative contracts (forwards, futures, swaps, and options), valuation models, and supporting market structures.
FINA 737.subject: FINA
FINA 737.title: Derivative Products and Analysis

FINA 738.description: Examines the important role that risk management, insurance, and finance have in dealing with climate change risk and how climate change risk affects financial markets and financial institutions.
FINA 738.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in DMSB 715 or FINA 760.
FINA 738.subject: FINA
FINA 738.title: Climate Change Risk Management, Insurance, and Finance

FINA 744.description: A study of non-speculative risk and risk bearing techniques, with emphasis on insurance covering personal, property, and liability risks. Attention is also given to the structure and regulation of the insurance industry, the role of governmental insurance programs, new product developments, and the impact of tort law reform, inflation, and consumerism.
FINA 744.subject: FINA
FINA 744.title: Risk and Insurance

FINA 745.description: An analytical study of group life, health, and retirement plans that provide economic security for employees; focuses on design, funding, tax considerations, cost controls, compliance with governmental regulations, the impact of inflation, and new types of benefits.
FINA 745.subject: FINA
FINA 745.title: Management of Employee Benefit Programs

FINA 746.description: Covers the concepts and tools businesses use when managing risk. Adopts an enterprise risk management perspective, i.e., considers a variety of risk exposures and methods for managing these risks. Main objective is to provide a decision-making framework applicable to different risk situations.
FINA 746.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 760 or DMSB 715.
FINA 746.subject: FINA
FINA 746.title: Risk Management

FINA 747.description: An intensive study of the financial planning process. Integration of insurance, investment, and tax principles in the development of comprehensive personal financial plans.
FINA 747.subject: FINA
FINA 747.title: Financial Planning Seminar

FINA 750.description: Fundamentals of analysis and decision making in financial management for human resource professionals.
FINA 750.subject: FINA
FINA 750.title: Finance for Human Resource Professionals

FINA 756.description: Analysis of financial statements for profitability and risk assessment and for firm and segment valuation.
FINA 756.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in DMSB 717 or ACCT 726 or ACCT 729 or equivalent.
FINA 756.subject: FINA
FINA 756.title: Financial Statement Analysis

FINA 760.description: Theory and fundamentals of analysis and decision-making in financial management.
FINA 760.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ACCT 725.
FINA 760.subject: FINA
FINA 760.title: Financial Policies

FINA 761.description: Advanced study of problems involved in the financial management of economic organizations.
FINA 761.subject: FINA
FINA 761.title: Advanced Financial Management

FINA 762.description: The use of analytical techniques to evaluate investment opportunities with consideration given to applicable quantitative methods of portfolio management.
FINA 762.subject: FINA
FINA 762.title: Investment Management

FINA 763.description: Applications of financial options in managing risk.
FINA 763.subject: FINA
FINA 763.title: Options in Corporate Finance

FINA 764.description: Characteristics, structure, and functions of money and capital markets; sources of funds for bond investment, stock financing, mortgage financing, and small business financing. Current problems and procedures in these markets are considered.
FINA 764.subject: FINA
FINA 764.title: Money and Capital Markets

FINA 765.description: Nature, functions, and operations of financial institutions with particular attention to the banking system. The activities of other lending and savings institutions are studied together with their monetary and fiscal implications.
FINA 765.subject: FINA
FINA 765.title: Management of Financial Institutions

FINA 766.description: A study of income producing properties including income expense analyses, capitalization processes and discount rates, direct capitalization methodologies, and computerized discounted cash flow valuation models.
FINA 766.subject: FINA
FINA 766.title: Advanced Real Estate Valuation

FINA 767.description: An analytical study of mortgage markets and the institutions involved. Particular emphasis is placed on specialized institutional practices, innovative financing techniques, and current developments.
FINA 767.subject: FINA
FINA 767.title: Real Estate Finance

FINA 768.description: Market analysis including an overview of market area study and its relationship to the feasibility of a specific project. Topics include theory and methods of market and feasibility analysis. Examples of market and feasibility studies are reviewed and critiqued.
FINA 768.subject: FINA
FINA 768.title: Real Estate Market Analysis

FINA 769.description: An integrative approach emphasizing the special features of real estate decisions; social, legal, economic, political, and environmental problems of the real estate sector within the economy as a whole are studied.
FINA 769.subject: FINA
FINA 769.title: Real Estate Decision and Administrative Processes

FINA 770.description: Fundamental principles of fixed-income securities and fixed-income valuation models, including valuation of bonds with embedded options.
FINA 770.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 762.
FINA 770.subject: FINA
FINA 770.title: Fixed-Income Securities

FINA 771.description: Analysis of the functions and operations of financial markets and institutions, focusing on insurance markets, investment banking, and market microstructure.
FINA 771.subject: FINA
FINA 771.title: Financial Services Markets and Institutions

FINA 772.description: Students will be introduced to a variety of approaches to security analysis and valuation techniques as they manage a real portfolio.
FINA 772.subject: FINA
FINA 772.title: Student-Managed Investments

FINA 773.description: Provide an understanding of the following: fundamentals of non-recourse, project financing; financial markets for project finance; infrastructure sectors and their business risks; transaction structures and the documentation used to structure individual project financing; political risk; currency risk and problems with respect to local currency financing; international organizations relevant to infrastructure investment and finance.
FINA 773.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 760 or DMSB 715.
FINA 773.subject: FINA
FINA 773.title: Project Finance

FINA 774.description: Explores the history, current environment, and near-term outlook of financial innovation (FinTech), focusing on applications of Blockchain technology and Machine Learning tools. The course is designed to provide hands on experience in writing a “smart contract” using a blockchain and in applying machine learning tools.
FINA 774.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in FINA 760 or DMSB 715.
FINA 774.subject: FINA
FINA 774.title: Financial Innovation

FINA 780.description: Exploration of the funding and financial management of emerging ventures, including sources and structure of capital, financial levers to drive performance and metrics to monitor performance, and the study of how to impact, capture, quantify and realize value.
FINA 780.subject: FINA
FINA 780.title: Entrepreneurial Finance and the Dynamics of Emerging Ventures

FINA 781.description: Advanced real estate investment analysis emphasizing equity investment positions under alternative ownership forms, syndications and securities registration, real estate productivity evaluation based on cash flow analysis, federal tax policies affecting real estate, and real estate portfolio analysis.
FINA 781.subject: FINA
FINA 781.title: Real Estate Investment Analysis

FINA 790.description: Analysis of current topics, issues and practices in various areas of finance.
FINA 790.subject: FINA
FINA 790.title: Special Topics in Finance

FINA 860.description: Fundamental concepts and issues in financial economics, such as risk aversion, portfolio theory, asset pricing models, arbitrage pricing models, corporate investment decisions, capital structure, dividend policy, risk management, and financial institutions.
FINA 860.subject: FINA
FINA 860.title: Principles of Finance

FINA 865.description: Utility models and various alternative models used in asset and security pricing. Emphasis is on seminal research in finance.
FINA 865.subject: FINA
FINA 865.title: Theory of Finance

FINA 866.description: Covers current theory of finance and extensions of the theoretical developments examined in FINA 865 Theory of Finance.
FINA 866.subject: FINA
FINA 866.title: Current Issues in Finance

FINA 867.description: Special topics in financial markets and institutions, investment and portfolio theory, and/or corporate finance that are not examined in FINA 865 or 866 .
FINA 867.subject: FINA
FINA 867.title: Advanced Topics in Finance

FINA 868.description: Planning and execution of applied research in finance.
FINA 868.subject: FINA
FINA 868.title: Empirical Methods in Financial Research

FINA 869.description: Examination of empirical literature in finance. Development of a research proposal is required.
FINA 869.subject: FINA
FINA 869.title: Seminar in Financial Research
